(1 comment)
But you haven't actually added error handling.  You've just caught the exception and blindly discarded it.
Sorry, I have already rewritten the commit.
If this pattern is _really_ something that needs to be copied as many times as you've copied it, something is seriously wrong with the `instanceIdDb` API.  Let's fix that instead.

I've updated `InstanceIdDb::next()` to return a `std::expected<uint8_t, int>`.
Does this solution address your concerns, or would you recommend a different approach?
Thanks in advance for your feedback.
Acknowledged
Don't use `what` for lg2 calls.
Done
expected<int-type, int-type> feels very unnatural to me.  @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au - opinions?
Yeaah, it doesn't seem great... having the error type inherit from `std::exception` would be better to eliminate subsequent type confusion.

I'm considering updating `InstanceIdDb::next()` to return `std::expected<uint8_t, InstanceIdError>`, where `InstanceIdError` would be a class derived from `std::exception` that contains both an error code and a message as members.
Would this API change address the concerns about error type clarity?
Yes. So, in cases where throwing an exception is a better thing to do (Most update logic) then you can just throw returnedThing;

Given we now have `std::expected` I'd rather we steer clear of thowing. Write the code to handle errors explicitly, and make conscious decisions about how they're handled. Much easier to reason about.

It's okay to explicitly punt on decisions too, just leave a log message and a comment about the trade-offs.

Thanks very much for the suggestion!
I've updated the implementation as per the previous feedback.
Do you have any further suggestions for modifications?
Acknowledged
We still have a blob of almost 10 lines of code that have to be duplicated though?
I'm not convinced this 10-line blob is even the behaviour we want - the caller can't know that the update process failed to start. Should we propagate the failure?

Would it be preferable to keep `InstanceIdDb::next()` returning an ID on success and throwing an exception on failure, but avoid catching exceptions at every call site—instead only handling them at the appropriate top-level logic?
Would this pattern for error propagation better match your expectations?
Acknowledged
Uh... what are we throwing?
Acknowledged

`const std::string&`

If you think that being able to move an r-value string is more efficient in some cases, create a separate r-value consuming constructor.
Won't be able to move once it is changed to `const std::string&`.

I've added both constructors: one taking const std::string& (copy) and one taking std::string&& (move) to support both cases efficiently.
Thank you very much!
Done

This is silently changing behavior.  We have to change all of these APIs to either throw like they use to or return the `expected` failure.

The way you've written this up, the caller has no idea that their operation was not completed correctly.

I agree with Patrick. My comment regarding log messages and comments was the backstop solution where it wasn't obvious what other course of action should be taken. But that's not the case here. This method should propagate the error and the call-site(s) should be updated to handle the unexpected case (and do so recursively as required).

I have changed the original void functions `sendActivateFirmwareRequest`, `sendUpdateComponentRequest`, `sendPassCompTableRequest`, and `startFwUpdateFlow` to return int error codes instead, and now propagate errors upwards via their return values.
Is this approach acceptable?

Because those methods (`sendActivateFirmwareRequest`, `sendUpdateComponentRequest`, `sendPassCompTableRequest`) are all invoked via a void callback, my current “return int” approach only lets me log and exit the callback—it still can’t bubble the error code back up.
Is it acceptable to leave it like this, or would you prefer that I revert to throwing an `InstanceIdError` inside the callback (and catch it in the top-level)?
Also, if it still needs to be propagated upwards, to which level should it be expected to propagate?"
For now, in `DeviceUpdater` and `InventoryManager`, I am handling errors by returning early and adding a TODO comment. Is this approach acceptable?
Is there a reason we can't throw the instance from the expected?

Gerrit CI (clang-tidy) complains because `std::expected::error()` returns a reference, so throwing it directly is unsafe.
I changed it to `throw InstanceIdError(instanceIdResult.error());` to throw a copy instead.
I noticed that `#include <system_error>` and `#include <cerrno>` are already present, so I believe there is no need to include them again.

These are changing in DeviceUpdater APIs return.
Can you separate these changing to different commit/

However, if I modify `instanceIdDb.next`, it will inevitably affect the way errors are handled in the DeviceUpdater part.
Could you please advise me on how to handle this to avoid the issue of blindly discarded errors mentioned earlier?
Thank you very much!
For now, in `DeviceUpdater` and `InventoryManager`, I am handling errors by returning early and adding a TODO comment. Is this approach acceptable?
The most simple way is just `return;` when `if (!instanceIdResult)` or in the error case. Then you can add other commit to return error code.

So, my current handling in `DeviceUpdater` and `InventoryManager` should already comply with the simple return approach.
For other parts, I am also returning or co_returning `PLDM_ERROR` directly in error cases.
Would you recommend adding TODO comments in all such places and addressing them in separate commits, or is there any other change you would suggest here?
Thank you for your feedback.

> So, my current handling in `DeviceUpdater` and `InventoryManager` should already comply with the simple return approach.

Sound great.

> For other parts, I am also returning or co_returning `PLDM_ERROR` directly in error cases.
> Would you recommend adding TODO comments in all such places and addressing them in separate commits, or is there any other change you would suggest here?

About todo, I don't think we need. Just add new commit to change APIs as you did in the old code on top this patch set.

> Thank you for your feedback.

I have removed all the TODO comments as suggested.
Does this meet your expectations?
Please let me know if there are any other areas you think need to be modified.
Thank you very much for your feedback!
I think these patterns can be eliminated by using a function template, which can spit out a log, return an error back to the caller or returns the value.

Could you kindly specify the format of the function template you are looking for? 
Additionally, could you let me know if we need to handle cases involving throw, return void, and return int?
Thank you very much.

If possible, I would appreciate clear guidance and examples to help me resolve the issue of avoiding core dumps when the pldmd instance ID is exhausted.
Thank you very much!

Okay, I understand. I will try to modify it this way first.
Thank you very much for your explanation.

Hi @manojkiran.eda@gmail.com

I made a slight change from your original suggestion.
Instead of returning only the error code (rc) from `getInstanceId`, I now have `InstanceIdDb::next()` construct a complete `InstanceIdError` (including a detailed error message) at the source.
Then, `getInstanceId` template function simply logs the error and propagates the full InstanceIdError object upward, rather than just returning the error code.

This approach gives more flexibility to the caller:
they can choose to handle the error code, access the full error message, or even throw the `InstanceIdError` further up the call stack, as needed.

Let me know if you have any concerns with this approach.
Yes, this sounds a lot better & cleaner than where we began.

Output message meets Anti-pattern in lg2: https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/anti-patterns.md#ill-defined-data-structuring-in-lg2-message-strings
Check the others output message also.
I will check it again

Since using lg2 in `utils.hpp` seems to require modifying the meson build files, I am currently still using `std::cerr` for error messages.
Do you think this is acceptable, or should I switch to using lg2 for logging?
nit : spacing.

This was caused by clang-format, so I simplified the description to avoid line wrapping.
Please let me know if there is anything else in this commit that needs to be modified in order to get it merged.
Thank you very much for your feedback!
We should keep this work, but throw the original exception type from the call-sites that can't yet be fixed.
